title: Isomorphisms of sheaf modules are local on an open covering
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $\mathcal O_X$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $X$, and $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ the category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For an open $U\subseteq X$ let $\mathcal O_U=\mathcal O_X|_U$ and, for an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal M$, let $\mathcal M|_U$ be the $\mathcal O_U$-module $W\mapsto\mathcal M(W)$ ($W\subseteq U$ open) with the restriction maps and module structures of $\mathcal M$ [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]; for a morphism $\alpha:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules let $\alpha|_U:\mathcal M|_U\to\mathcal N|_U$ be the morphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules with components $(\alpha|_U)_W=\alpha_W$ for $W\subseteq U$ open. A morphism is an isomorphism if it has a two-sided inverse in the category of modules in question. Let $X=\bigcup_{a\in A}U_a$ be an open covering and $\alpha:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ a morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Then $\alpha$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules if and only if $\alpha|_{U_a}:\mathcal M|_{U_a}\to\mathcal N|_{U_a}$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{U_a}$-modules for every $a\in A$.

proof.text: *Step 1 (restriction is a functor).* For opens $V\subseteq U\subseteq X$ and morphisms $\alpha:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$, $\beta:\mathcal N\to\mathcal P$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules: $(\beta\circ\alpha)|_U=\beta|_U\circ\alpha|_U$, $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal M}|_U=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal M|_U}$, and $(\alpha|_U)|_V=\alpha|_V$ (with $(\mathcal M|_U)|_V=\mathcal M|_V$). Indeed all of these have the same component at every open $W\subseteq U$ (resp. $W\subseteq V$), namely $\beta_W\circ\alpha_W$, $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal M(W)}$, $\alpha_W$, by the definition of restriction in the statement; and morphisms of sheaves of modules with equal components are equal [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 04TN (lemma-glue-maps, line 5078) and its proof (Section 00AK)

proof.text: *Step 2 (only if).* Let $\beta:\mathcal N\to\mathcal M$ be an inverse of $\alpha$: $\beta\circ\alpha=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal M}$, $\alpha\circ\beta=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal N}$. Restricting these equalities to $U_a$ and using Step 1 gives $\beta|_{U_a}\circ\alpha|_{U_a}=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal M|_{U_a}}$ and $\alpha|_{U_a}\circ\beta|_{U_a}=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal N|_{U_a}}$, so $\alpha|_{U_a}$ is an isomorphism with inverse $\beta|_{U_a}$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 04TN (lemma-glue-maps, line 5078) and its proof (Section 00AK)

proof.text: *Step 3 (the local inverses agree on overlaps).* Assume each $\alpha|_{U_a}$ is an isomorphism and let $\beta_a:\mathcal N|_{U_a}\to\mathcal M|_{U_a}$ be its inverse. Fix $a,b\in A$ and put $U_{ab}=U_a\cap U_b$. By Step 1, $(\alpha|_{U_a})|_{U_{ab}}=\alpha|_{U_{ab}}=(\alpha|_{U_b})|_{U_{ab}}$, and restricting $\beta_a\circ\alpha|_{U_a}=\mathrm{id}$, $\alpha|_{U_a}\circ\beta_a=\mathrm{id}$ to $U_{ab}$ shows that $\beta_a|_{U_{ab}}$ is a two-sided inverse of $\alpha|_{U_{ab}}$; likewise $\beta_b|_{U_{ab}}$. A two-sided inverse is unique: if $\gamma,\gamma'$ are both inverse to $\alpha|_{U_{ab}}$ then $\gamma=\gamma\circ(\alpha|_{U_{ab}}\circ\gamma')=(\gamma\circ\alpha|_{U_{ab}})\circ\gamma'=\gamma'$. Hence $\beta_a|_{U_{ab}}=\beta_b|_{U_{ab}}$ for all $a,b\in A$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 04TN (lemma-glue-maps, line 5078) and its proof (Section 00AK)

proof.text: *Step 4 (glue the inverses).* By Step 3, the $\mathcal O_{U_a}$-linear maps $\beta_a:\mathcal N|_{U_a}\to\mathcal M|_{U_a}$ satisfy $\beta_a|_{U_{ab}}=\beta_b|_{U_{ab}}$ for all $a,b$. By [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules] (1), applied to the covering $X=\bigcup_aU_a$ with $\mathcal F=\mathcal N$, $\mathcal G=\mathcal M$, $\varphi_a=\beta_a$, there is an $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\beta:\mathcal N\to\mathcal M$ with $\beta|_{U_a}=\beta_a$ for every $a\in A$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 04TN (lemma-glue-maps, line 5078) and its proof (Section 00AK)

proof.text: *Step 5 ($\beta$ is inverse to $\alpha$).* For every $a$, Step 1 gives $(\beta\circ\alpha)|_{U_a}=\beta_a\circ\alpha|_{U_a}=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal M|_{U_a}}=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal M}|_{U_a}$ and $(\alpha\circ\beta)|_{U_a}=\alpha|_{U_a}\circ\beta_a=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal N}|_{U_a}$. By the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules] (1) (two $\mathcal O_X$-linear maps that agree on every member of an open covering are equal), $\beta\circ\alpha=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal M}$ and $\alpha\circ\beta=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal N}$. Hence $\alpha$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules with inverse $\beta$.
